1.

The accused/applicant has preferred this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure for releasing him on regular bail in connection with Crime No. 163 / 2023
registered at Police Station Shivrinarayan, Distt. Janjgir-Champa (C.G.) for commission of offence
punishable under Sections 376, 506-B, 34 and 120-B of the Ipc.
2.

Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that in the month of October, 2020 when victim/prosecutrix,
who is young girl, aged about 22 years, in her house alone, then applicant went there and sexually Aakash Yadav vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2877538/
1 exploited her by threatening her.

sentences.text: It is further alleged that on being complaint made by Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:28541 victim/prosecutrix to mother of the applicant, she said that she made her (victim/prosecutrix) daughter-in-law, thereafter,applicant again and again sexually exploited her.
It is further alleged that mother of the applicant also used to threaten her to kill her family members.
Subsequently, some dispute arose between applicant and the victim/prosecutrix,

therefore, present FIR was lodged by the victim/prosecutrix against the applicant, his mother and other family members and the applicant was arrested on 17.07.2023.
3.

Learned counsel appearing for the applicant would submit that victim/prosecutrix and applicant are resident of same place i.e. Ward No. 8, Shivrinarayan, District Janjgir-Champa and they were in love relation for about 2  years and in between they have also made consensual physical relation,
subsequently, their relation became soured and due to that victim/prosecutrix posted some objectionable photographs of mother and sister of the applicant in the social media, hence, mother of the applicant lodged FIR against the present applicant being Crime No. 29/2023, and as a counter blast, victim/prosecutrix has lodged present FIR against the applicant.

He further submits that mother, father and sister of the applicant have already been granted anticipatory bail by the Sessions Court; charge-sheet has already been filed and the applicant is in jail since 17.07.2023; and,
therefore, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
4.

Per contra, learned counsel for the State, who is well assisted by counsel for the Objector/complainant, would submit that applicant had sexually exploited the victim/prosecutrix by cheating her on the pretext Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:28541 of marriage and subsequently, he refused to marry her.

It is further submitted that the since applicant is political influential persons,
therefore, he is threatening her, hence, applicant is not entitled for bail.
5.
I have heard learend counsel appearing for the parties and perused the case diary.

6. Having heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the material available on record, particularly considering the fact that victim/prosecutrix was major lady at the time of incident and she had long relation with the applicant; charge-sheet has already been filed and the applicant is in custody since 17.07.2023; I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.
7. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on regular bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one local surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the trial Court on the following conditions that :
a) Applicant shall appear before the trial Court regularly on each and every date,
unless exempted from appearance.
b) Applicant shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c) If the applicant is found involved in similar offence in the future it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of Bail.
